cases.title: Paid Commission for DPOs | Contribute to sector-changing research on DPO Funding

two_main_points.point: Partners are conducting UK-wide research into disability-sector and DPO funding, intended to support campaigning for funding justice.
DPOs are invited to verify their details through a paid 30-minute form.

verified_facts.fact: Trust for London, Disability Rights UK and Braw Data are collaborating on UK-wide research mapping funding to the disability sector and Disabled People's Organisations.
The partners state that the research is intended to support campaigners promoting funding justice for Disabled People's Organisations and led-by-and-for organisations.
Disabled People's Organisations are offered £50 to complete a 30-minute form confirming their classification and funding sources.
The research and funding map are still being assembled; the source does not report that funding transparency or justice has already improved.

cases.title: BCA calls for calm in smart glasses ban debate

two_main_points.point: Blind Citizens Australia is responding to proposed smart-glasses bans and explaining their assistive use by blind and partially sighted people.
Users report feeling unsafe, while some councils have introduced ad hoc facility bans.

verified_facts.fact: Blind Citizens Australia warns that calls to ban smart glasses are putting blind and partially sighted people in danger.
The organisation describes smart glasses as assistive technology that can combine several platforms in one wearable device.
Members and other users report feeling unsafe using the devices in public, while some councils have introduced ad hoc bans at facilities.
verified_facts.evidence_ref: publisher article, reported experiences and council actions

verified_facts.fact: The source does not establish that all smart glasses are assistive or that a nationwide ban exists.

cases.title: ConnectAbility: Building Digital Inclusion Through Virtual Services and Assistive Technology

two_main_points.point: ConnectAbility is a two-year project exploring how adult disability services can provide virtual services alongside face-to-face support.
Its team has produced a resource of assistive technologies, accessibility tools, apps, guides and supports for neurodivergent and intellectually disabled people.

verified_facts.fact: ConnectAbility is a two-year initiative focused on adult disability services and virtual services.
The project seeks to explore and enhance services' capacity to offer virtual services as a complementary model rather than replace face-to-face services.
The team developed an Assistive Technology for Digital Inclusion resource covering tools, apps, guides and supports for neurodivergent or intellectually disabled people.
The project says it will produce a replicable framework for HSE-funded day services; the framework is not reported as complete.

cases.title: Using Puck.js to Answer a Mobile Phone Call

two_main_points.point: The article demonstrates configuring Puck.js as an accessible switch for people with limited mobility to answer an Android phone call.
A Bluetooth volume-up command triggers Android's answer-call setting, while iPhones require a different auto-answer feature.

verified_facts.fact: The demonstration uses a programmable Bluetooth Puck.js device as an accessible switch to answer an incoming mobile phone call.
The approach is presented for people with limited mobility or reduced hand function who may find a touchscreen difficult to reach or use quickly.
Puck.js sends a Bluetooth volume-up command and Android's accessibility setting uses that command to answer the call.
The same method does not answer calls on an iPhone; the article instead points to Apple's built-in Auto-Answer Calls feature.
The author says the device is highly programmable but criticises its switch for requiring pressure on a specific area.

cases.title: V&A's Design and Disability with a Scottish accent: a call to action

two_main_points.point: A review examines V&A Dundee's reconfigured Design and Disability exhibition celebrating disabled-led design with Scottish additions.
The exhibition includes about 170 objects and several access measures, though the reviewer identifies limits in touch access and representation.

verified_facts.fact: V&A Dundee hosts a reconfigured Design and Disability exhibition celebrating disabled-led design across art, architecture, fashion, photography and design.
The Dundee presentation adds Scottish artists and designers to material adapted from the London exhibition.
About 170 objects from the 1940s to the present are organised around Visibility, Creativity and Living.
The reviewer notes BSL and audio-described tours, large-print guides, DeafSpace-style mirrors and some tactile exhibits, but says touch remains limited and not all impairment types are represented.

cases.title: A new chapter for Disability Arts Online: Kate Lovell named as Artistic Director

two_main_points.point: Disability Arts Online has appointed disabled and neurodivergent theatre-maker Kate Lovell as its first Artistic Director.
She will lead its talent development and creative programmes, including the magazine, and co-lead the organisation with its chief executive.

verified_facts.fact: Disability Arts Online announced Kate Lovell as its first Artistic Director.
Lovell is a disabled and neurodivergent theatre-maker, playwright and social justice activist.
In the role, Lovell will lead talent development and creative programmes, including the magazine, and co-lead the organisation with chief executive Trish Wheatley.
She previously participated in the organisation's disabled writers' programme and later contributed to its magazine and podcast.
